content.text: The code takes a cookie value, decodes it, and passes it into a shell command via ProcessBuilder with "sh -c echo <bar>". This is a genuine command injection vulnerability - the switch statement always flows to case 'A' (since switchTarget is 'C' based on "ABC".charAt(2)), so bar = param (tainted value from cookie).

input.justification: The doPost method reads a cookie value (user-controlled), URL-decodes it into `param`, then assigns it to `bar` via a switch statement. Since guess="ABC" and switchTarget=guess.charAt(2)='C', the 'C'/'D' case is taken, so bar=param (tainted). This tainted string is concatenated into "echo " + bar and passed as part of the command list to ProcessBuilder, which then executes via a shell (sh -c / cmd.exe /c). No sanitization or escaping is performed on the cookie value before it's embedded in the shell command string, allowing shell metacharacters (e.g., ; | & $()) in the cookie value to inject arbitrary commands. This matches the classic OWASP Benchmark command injection pattern and is a true positive.
